key_impacts: Washed away 243,191 houses nationwide; 370,587 houses partially damaged.
3,520 houses washed away and 1,800 partially damaged in Dakshin Bedkashi.
Coastal embankment overtopped and breached at six points; 20.55 km of 27.37 km damaged.
Villages inundated twice daily by tidal water until polder rehabilitation in 2013, delaying recovery.
evidence_snippets: Cyclone Aila hit the Bangladesh coast on 25 May 2009 with 65-knot winds and a 2–6 m storm surge.
In Dakshin Bedkashi, Aila and storm surge killed 33 people and washed away 3,520 houses; 1,800 houses partially damaged.
Storm surge breached the coastal embankment in six places; 20.55 km damaged of 27.37 km; villages inundated twice daily until 2013.
missing_information: Comprehensive national casualties and losses beyond Koyra.
Precise geospatial extent of flooding outside the named locations.

key_impacts: Described as a devastating cyclone in 2007.
Prompted government prioritization of housing recovery.
Post-Sidr housing recovery failed to improve safety from cyclone hazard, per authors.
evidence_snippets: Bangladesh government prioritized housing recovery after two recent devastating cyclones: Sidr (2007) and Aila (2009).
Failure of post-Sidr housing recovery to improve cyclone safety influenced this research.
